Sidebar revealed (âŒ˜â‡§S), terminal | browser split, âŒ˜K open. The 30px top strip keeps identity and window controls when the sidebar is hidden.
Spaces are windows: the Space row at the top of the sidebar is a window switcher (âŒ˜âŒ¥1â€“9); the tab list is this Space only.
Wordmark: Newsreader Italic. UI face and terminal face are both config keys (default IBM Plex Mono).

CHROMELESS â€” the default. Full-bleed terminal, a 4px hot edge where the sidebar hides. The localhost hook is a ruled chip anchored to the detected line (âŒ˜â†µ split, âŒ˜â‡§â†µ new tab). Attention state surfaces in the top strip, not as a popup.
QUICK TERMINAL â€” âŒ¥âŒ˜T drops a sheet from the top edge over whatever is focused (here a browser tab in the blue 'work' Space). Same 2px edge + hard shadow as the palette.
PIP â€” our own always-on-top window drawing a tab's texture: a video (left) or a terminal tab you're keeping an eye on (right). Signal band shows which Space it came from; â†— returns it to its tab.

TOKENS â€” what spike 4 renders from: paper/ink for both themes, six Space signals, ANSI 0â€“15 per theme, type ramp (IBM Plex Mono + Instrument Serif wordmark), rule weights, spacing, states, keys, principles.
Direction pass, kept for the record. Broadsheet was chosen; Aurora and Instrument are not being built.

SIDEBAR â€” third pass. Hover the left edge to reveal; hides ~300 ms after the mouse leaves; Ctrl+Shift+S pins.
Space row = window switcher. Pinned row. Compact rows (number Â· kind glyph Â· title Â· cwd/host); the 52px preview expands only under the hovered row (03) and under a waiting tab (02).
Footer: Space avatar + name + browser identity, shell profile row, assistant router row, + new tab / settings.

SETTINGS TAB â€” Ctrl+, opens a native tab. Sections left; key / control rows right (ruled segmented switches, boxed fields). Every change writes ~/.config/nus/init.luau, shown live at the bottom; the file stays the source of truth.

LOOK & FEEL — settings, eighth pass (proposal).
The nav gains two groups: LOOK (surface · theme · rules · cursor) and FEEL (motion · sound · startup). Every page: sections left, key / control rows right, a live proof on the far right, and the file it writes named at the bottom of the nav. Nothing here is a token change — Broadsheet stays fixed; these are the user's levers on top of it.

SURFACE — signal + ordered stops (gradient/aurora run through them), a family strip derived from the signal, base + tint, opacity (panes · chrome · window), texture (grain · stipple · stitch · linen · halftone; strength, scale, where), carapace style/width/radius/angle, aurora drift & breath. Presets save the whole card; surface.luau is the file.

THEME — the two papers' tokens with derived ones following unless pinned; contrast read out live; ANSI 0–15 editable or from a family; proof in a shell; import from Ghostty / iTerm / VS Code / Windows Terminal / base16.

RULES — the file is the page: syntax-coloured, a starter set (hue per tab · family per stack · by host · monochrome · time of day), a live sidebar showing what the rules do now, and a scratch call. A fourth hook, on_event, lets rules pick sounds.

SOUND — cuelume's seventeen cues, ported into the app as recipes (tone / noise layers, envelope, glide, shimmer) and synthesized natively; each drawn as its shape. Right: event → cue or quiet. Volume, quiet hours, your own recipes in sound.luau. MIT, credited.

STARTUP — the launch as a sequence: window (last · maximized · fullscreen · centered) → splash (draws in · still · none, hold min/max) → then (restore · shell · page · nothing) → atlas (planet · also at launch · persistent). Sound with the splash; links from outside; start at login.

CURSOR — shape, blink policy, colour (ink · signal · the tab's own · custom), motion (jump · glide · comet trail on the motion register), beam width; the pointer over the chrome; hide while typing. Drawn by nus, not the shell.

Sidebar header — three directions. Windows, not spaces; the name is the title the wordmark was holding; NEW TAB is the button hit most. Approve one or name the amalgam (e.g. Masthead title + Ledger next-row + Spine on hover).

Tab drag — three directions for one tab director. Five things a drag can do: move (around tabs), stack (in / out), join (multiplex into another tab as a pane), tile (beside, on the page), send (to another window); plus copy.
A chooses the verb by place, B by waiting, C by key. Common ground (bottom right) holds what all three share: one Intent drawn by ghost, target and words alike; bounds with hysteresis; dwell only when still; the Wayland gap.
Suggested amalgam: A's lanes and quarters as the base, C's director bar plus shift = join and 1–9 = send, and B's dwell only for folded stacks and the window name. Approve one or name the mix.

Tab state — three directions for what's inside a tab or a stack, on the same nine tabs. A states it in a fixed cell, B shows the tab itself (live crops, a hover card), C writes a line of words only when there's news, with a shaped edge.
Suggested mix: C's wire and edge at rest, A's spine for folded stacks, B's hover card on demand. Approve one or name the mix.

Bookmarks — one store for everything kept. Today six places keep a link (pins, folders, the reading list, saved commands, notes' sources, history); here they become one record with roles: in (collections), pin, to read, keyword, copy, quote, and here (personal or this project). One verb, ⌘D; one mark, the ribbon.
A browses in the sidebar, B on one Library page, C nowhere: ⌘D keeps, ⌘K finds. Common ground (bottom right) holds the record, the verb, the bands and the two homes.
Suggested mix: C's verb and recall everywhere (kept leads the palette and the address field), B's Library as the one place to tidy (the reading-list page grown up), and from A only Pinned and This project in the sidebar. Approve one or name the mix.

Notifications: three systems for sites that have news (mail, chat, calendars, GitHub, feeds). A listens to the open page: its notifications, its badge, the count in its title, with nothing to set up. B is a Desk fed by protocols, with no page running. C is lines: a small signed file per service, plus a switchboard that routes channels and holds them while you're busy.
Common ground (bottom right) holds the notice record, its place on the tab-state ladder, and the research that sets the limits: CEF has no Notification API and no Web Push, hidden pages slow down, and Gmail and 365 want OAuth.
Suggested mix: A as the base (the shim and listening tabs, because every option needs the shim), C's switchboard and hold without lines at first, and from B only nus notify and GitHub. Approve one or name the mix.

Downloads: three ways to show that a download happened and where it went, which is the downloads icon in the sidebar’s foot. The sidebar is usually hidden, so each option also has to work against the hot edge. A sends the file there (a slip slides into the edge), B draws a rule there and makes the window’s foot the progress bar, C brings the place to you (the sidebar’s foot peeks out with the file on it).
Common ground (bottom right): motion only when you started it, never toward a place that isn’t drawn, the icon’s underline fills by bytes, reduced motion keeps the state and drops the travel.
Suggested mix: A’s slip for the click, landing in the corner and becoming B’s foot rule for the duration; C’s peek only for your first three downloads, as the lesson. Approve one or name the mix.

Hatch at rest: three ways to draw the closed hatch where there is no notch (Windows, Linux, Macs on other displays). Today that’s a 330 × 30 bar reading “Hatch · ready”. A is only the lip: a 5 px seam with a segment per piece of work. B is the sheet rolled up: a 19 px tab of lamps, each one a button. C is the mark: the icon’s orbit on a cord, turning while work runs and stopping when something needs you.
Common ground (bottom right): what others do (Dynamic Island, notch apps, quake terminals, the Windows top edge, calm technology, the dark cockpit), one set of marks for all three, and the rules.
Suggested mix: A at rest, lowering into B’s tab when you reach for it, so it stays 5 px until you want the lamps. C as a second look later. Chosen 2026-10-09: B, Lamps, on its own (built in hatch_lamps.rs). The orbit stays on the page.
